chunks: Al-Hakim Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Maruzi narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Jarjani narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Abd al-Samad ibn Yahya al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Madani narrated from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), that he said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, created the Light of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his Family) before He created the heavens and the earth, the Throne, the Chair, the Tablet, the Pen, Paradise and the Fire, and before He created Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub, Musa, Isa, Dawud, Sulayman and everyone about whom Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, mentioned in His saying: 'And We gave to him Ishaq and Ya'qub...' until His saying: '...and We guided them to a straight path', and before He created all the Prophets by four hundred and twenty thousand years. And He, Exalted and Glorious is He, created with it twelve Covers: the Cover of Ability, the Cover of Greatness, the Cover of Favor, the Cover of Mercy, the Cover of Happiness, the Cover of Dignity, the Cover of the Rank, the Cover of Guidance, the Cover of Prophethood, the Cover of Loftiness, the Cover of Prestige, and the Cover of Salvation,

Then He restrained the Light of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his Family) in the Cover of Ability for twelve thousand years, while it was saying: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Highest'; and in the Cover of Greatness for eleven thousand years, while it was saying: 'Glory be to the Knower of the Secret'; and in the Cover of Favor for ten thousand years, while it was saying: 'Glory be to He who is Subsistent and does not amuse Himself'; and in the Cover of Mercy for nine thousand years, while it was saying: 'Glory be to the Lofty, the Highest'; and in the Cover of Happiness for eight thousand years, while it was saying: 'Glory be to He who is Everlasting and does not omit'; and in the Cover of Dignity for seven thousand years, while it was saying: 'Glory be to He who is Self-Sufficient and does not need'; and in the Cover of the Rank for six thousand years, while it was saying: 'Glory be to the All-Knowing, the All-Generous'; and in the Cover of Guidance for five thousand years, while it was saying: 'Glory be to the One with the Great Throne'; and in the Cover of Prophethood for four thousand years, while it was saying: 'Glory be to the Lord of Might above what they describe'; and in the Cover of Loftiness for three thousand years, while it was saying: 'Glory be to the One with Ownership and Kingdom'; and in the Cover of Prestige for two thousand years, while it was saying: 'Glory be to Allah, and in Praise of Him'; and in the Cover of Salvation for a thousand years, while it was saying: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Great, and in Praise of Him'.

Then He made his name appear on the Tablet, and he remained enlightened on the Tablet for four thousand years. Then He made him appear on the Throne, and so, he was by the leg of the Throne, fastened, for seven thousand years until Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, placed him in the backbone of Adam (peace be upon him), and then He transmitted him from the backbone of Adam to the backbone of Nuh (peace be upon him), and then from one backbone to another backbone, until Allah, Exalted is He, took him out of the backbone of Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib. Then, He generously dignified him with six miracles: He made him wear the Shirt of Satisfaction; dressed him with the Garment of Prestige; throned him with the Crown of Guidance; made him wear the Trousers of Conscious Knowledge; made his waistband the Waistband of Love, by which he tightens his trousers; made his sandal the Sandal of Fear; and He handed to him the Staff of the Rank,

Then He said to him: O Muhammad, go to the people and say to them: Say: 'There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah'. The making of that shirt was from six things: its figure was of ruby; its sleeves were of pearl; its patch was of yellow crystal; its underarms was of peridot; its collar was of red corals; and its pocket was of the Light of the Lord, Glorified be His Glory. Allah accepted the repentance of Adam (peace be upon him) by that shirt, returned the ring of Sulayman with it, returned Yusuf to Ya'qub with it, saved Yunus from the belly of the whale with it, and so with the rest of the Prophets (peace be upon them). He saved them from misfortunes with it, and that shirt was not but the shirt of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his Family).

key_terms.تَكَةَ الْمَحَبَّةِ: The Waistband of Love, symbolizing the bond of divine love
key_terms.حِجَاب: Cover or veil, a spiritual station or layer of divine manifestation
key_terms.سِتُّ كَرَامَاتٍ: The six miracles or dignities bestowed upon the Prophet
key_terms.صَلْبُ آدَمَ: The backbone of Adam, referring to the lineage of prophetic transmission
key_terms.قَمِيصُ الرِّضَا: The Shirt of Satisfaction, a symbol of divine acceptance
key_terms.نُورُ مُحَمَّدٍ: The Light of Muhammad, the primordial essence of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What are the six spiritual garments and their meanings in the hadith of the Light of Muhammad?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* articulates the Shia doctrine of *Al-Nur al-Muhammadi* (the Muhammadan Light), emphasizing its pre-eternal existence within twelve divine veils before descending through the lineage of Prophets. It highlights the continuity of prophetic authority by linking the specific spiritual garments of Muhammad (peace be upon him) to the miracles of earlier prophets, such as Solomon’s ring and Joseph’s return, thereby establishing his unique ontological status in Shia cosmology.
